title: S corporation distributions and gifts — Tom Ridge
instructions: Tom Ridge owns 100% of Ridge Inc., a calendar-year S corporation that was a C corporation until 2021. Compute his 2025 amounts, then answer the gift tax questions.

exhibits.title: Ridge Inc. — 2025
exhibits.content:
- Accumulated E&P from C corporation years: **$12,000**
- AAA at January 1, 2025: **$20,000**
- 2025 ordinary business income: **$50,000**
- 2025 tax-exempt interest: **$3,000**
- Tom's stock basis at January 1, 2025: **$40,000**
- Distribution to Tom on December 31, 2025: **$90,000**

exhibits.title: Tom's 2025 gifts (Tom's wife consents to gift splitting)
exhibits.content:
- $50,000 cash to his daughter
- $20,000 paid directly to a hospital for his mother's surgery
- $100,000 of stock to his wife (a U.S. citizen)

rows.label: AAA available before the distribution
rows.explanation: 20,000 + 50,000 ordinary income = **70,000** (tax-exempt income doesn't increase AAA).

rows.label: Dividend portion of the distribution
rows.explanation: After 70,000 from AAA, the next 12,000 comes from accumulated E&P.

rows.label: Tom's ending stock basis
rows.explanation: 93,000 − 70,000 (AAA) − 8,000 (remaining amount from basis) = **15,000**; the dividend portion doesn't reduce basis.

rows.label: Tom's taxable gift to his daughter (after splitting)
Taxable gift from paying the hospital
rows.explanation: Medical expenses paid directly are excluded: **0**.

parts.prompt: Eligibility — does each event terminate Ridge Inc.'s S election?

rows.label: Tom sells 10% of his shares to a partnership
rows.explanation: A partnership is an ineligible shareholder.

rows.label: Ridge issues nonvoting common stock with identical distribution rights
rows.explanation: Voting differences don't create a second class of stock.
